Subject: SLO qualification: warm-pool activation matrix & demo commitments

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps to get to a short technical demo and an SLO sanity check: 

Summary of customer targets you gave today:
- 95th percentile latency (single-turn, non-streaming): <= 300 ms
- Streaming token latency requirement: <= 150 ms per token (for audio-transcription style callouts)
- Sustained throughput: 200 req/s during business hours; burst capacity to 1,200 concurrent requests for marketing push events
- Acceptable cold-start window for new instances: <= 60s; prefer ~30s warm-up for critical routes

What we propose as next steps (I recommend we treat this as a short MSA milestoned mutual action plan):
1) I'll send a warm-pool activation matrix (attached) describing prewarmed instance counts and expected scale-up times for the mix you described.
2) Monica will validate streaming token-latency assumptions and provide a lightweight priming sample (logs + config) for your team to run in a staging window.
3) Rishi will run a quick concurrency stress test against a representative model variant to show queueing behavior and tail latency under burst.
4) Schedule a 45-min technical demo next week (I propose Wed 3/16 10:00 PT).

Attachments: warm_pool_activation_matrix.xlsx (single-sheet summary), sample-priming-logs.txt

Please reply with any corrections to the targets above or if you want a different demo cadence. If that schedule works, I’ll send the invite and the test credentials.

—Michael

Thanks Michael — that summary matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 1,200 concurrent number is for peak marketing-driven spikes (lasting ~3–8 minutes) and will be focused on a small set of routes (customer-facing chat + notifications).
- For streaming, the 150 ms target is ideal; if you can demonstrate consistent <200 ms token latency with graceful degradation, that would be acceptable.
- Cold-starts are expected to be rare, but we need documented behavior if a warm-pool fails (fallback to queued requests with SLA on first-response).

Wed 3/16 10:00 PT works. Please include your solutions engineer and an ops contact so we can talk queueing and retry semantics.

On Wed, Mar 9, 2027 at 5:22 PM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monica: can you prepare a short priming script (single-file curl-based example) that demonstrates token-streaming and captures client-observed per-token latency? Attach logs and expected config.

Hi all — attaching a priming sample and a short readme in the Drive link. Quick technical notes for the demo: 
- Priming approach: warm the model with a 6-token prefix and a short batch of synthetic calls; we expect streaming steady-state token latency ~90–140 ms on nv4-equivalent instances; non-streaming 95p should be in the 250–350 ms range depending on sequence length.
- Warm-pool sizing recommendation for your traffic mix (from my local sim): 8 prewarmed instances for critical routes, 12 for the full-marketing route set to hit ~1,200 concurrent with acceptable tail.
- Scale-up timeline: hot start (reuse KV cache) ~8–12s; cold start (new container + model load) ~45–70s depending on quantization profile.
- Queueing policy we’ll demo: short-lived in-memory queue with head-of-line priority for low-latency routes; we’ll show the effect of backpressure with a 95% rejected-threshold after sustained overload.

I’ll bring the script and the sample logs to the call.

—Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Alex Burton <alex.burton@fastbank.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO qualification: warm-pool activation matrix & demo commitments

Alex / Michael — quick operational confirmation ahead of the demo: 
- I ran a quick concurrency sweep on a representative model in staging using your approximate request mix. Results (summary):
  * Sustained 200 req/s: 95p latency ~220 ms, 99p ~380 ms when sequence length <=128 tokens.
  * Burst to 1,200 concurrent (sustained 3 min): with 12 prewarmed instances, queueing kept 95p latency ~360 ms; without warm pool, tail spikes exceed 1s until new instances finish startup.
- Failover behavior: if a warm instance fails, we fallback to available pool and enqueue with an exponential backoff policy; we’ll show how we surface this in traces and the Console.
- For the demo, I’ll include a quick run that toggles warm-pool size (4 / 8 / 12) and shows the latency curves + queue depth traces so you can see tradeoffs live.

See you on the call. I’ve uploaded the raw run artifacts to the Drive link in case you want to inspect before the demo.

—Rishi
SRE Lead (Redwood Inference)
